subject: Dedicated capacity: GPU bands, throughput targets & budget — next steps
messages:
From: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@brightanalytics.com>
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@brightanalytics.com
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: dedicated capacity options — clarifying throughput & budget

Rafael — thanks for the discovery call earlier. Quick recap and a couple of clarifying items so we can prepare an apples-to-apples quote: 

- Target workload: real-time customer chat generation (single-turn + short context).
- Typical response size: 120–320 tokens (mean ~200).
- Concurrent request pattern today: spiky; expect peak 80–150 rps, steady-state 40–70 rps.
- Monthly token volume: we estimate 600M–1.1B input+output tokens to start, could grow 2–3x in 12 months.
- Security/procurement: we need a private deployment or dedicated (VPC) with SOC2 evidence.
- Budget band: preliminary ops budget is $30k–$80k/month for inference (we can be flexible depending on TCO).

Questions for you:
1) Can you sketch two commitment bands (conservative and aggressive) with recommended GPU families (A100 vs H100), expected sustained throughput for each band, and a ballpark $/1M tokens number so we can check viability?
2) Is a single-GPU pilot viable to validate latency/quality before committing a reserved pool?

I attached our internal SOW overview and a simple throughput table (we'll send the procurement contact if/when we move).

Thanks,
Aisha
Head of ML Ops
BrightAnalytics

---
Attachments: BrightAnalytics_RH_SOW_v1.pdf (pdf), throughput-estimate.xlsx (xlsx)
From: rafael_mendes@redwood.com
To: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@brightanalytics.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 09:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: dedicated capacity options — clarifying throughput & budget

Thanks Aisha — appreciated the clear summary. Below is a concise options matrix and next steps so you can share with procurement and engineering. I'll produce a formal quote after you confirm which band you prefer and whether you'd like a pilot.

High-level recommendation (two bands):

Band A — conservative commit (lower unit cost, more reserved capacity)
- Hardware: H100 (80GB) reserved pool
- Typical pool size we recommend for your 600M/mo baseline: 4 x H100 (reserved) with burst headroom 
- Expected sustained throughput: ~140–200 rps (depending on batch/queuing, 200 tokens avg)
- Ballpark unit econ: ~$450–$650 per 1M tokens (this includes infra amortization + Redwood support & observability)
- Notes: best for predictable latency and growth to >1B tokens/mo; higher upfront commit.

Band B — lower upfront (flexible)
- Hardware: A100 80GB or A10G (cost-optimized)
- Recommended: 6 x A100 or 8 x A10G (reserved smaller instance types to handle spikes)
- Expected sustained throughput: ~90–140 rps (same token assumptions)
- Ballpark unit econ: ~$600–$900 per 1M tokens (depends on quantization and batching)
- Notes: cheaper reservation, more instances to achieve throughput; slightly higher unit cost at scale.

Pilot option
- Single H100 (or 2 A100) pilot for 2–4 weeks to validate latency, KV-cache warmup, and prefix caching benefits. Pilot pricing can be discounted and applied to committed months once you sign a reservation.

Risk / tradeoffs
- H100 gives headroom for lower p99 latency and better packing for quantized models; higher capital cost but lower unit token cost at scale.
- A100/A10G trades off single-GPU latency for lower reservation fees.

Requested confirmations from your side:
1) Preferred band (A or B) and target committed months (6/12/24).
2) Whether you want a pilot (single H100) and preferred start week.
3) Any firm target for $/1M tokens you must hit to proceed (helps prioritize sizing).

Next steps: once you confirm, Marissa will run an internal throughput simulation and share a CSV with expected rps/latency for the two bands, and we'll push a formal quote + draft RA (reservation agreement).

Cheers,
Rafael Mendes
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

---
Attachments referenced: redwood-dedicated-options.csv
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 10:22:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: throughput sims and model notes for BrightAnalytics (internal)

Rafael / Neha — I ran the quick sims against their token distribution and the model family they mentioned (Llama-derivative, ~70B param). Key notes below (pasting for thread continuity):

- With H100 x4 (80GB), expected sustained throughput with q4/q8 quantization: ~160–190 rps at 200 token mean, p95 latency ~220–320 ms depending on batching.
- A100 x6 gives ~110–140 rps; p95 ~280–380 ms.
- Prefix caching should cut token compute by ~20–30% for repeated contexts (they said many short, repetitive prompts).
- Cost sensitivity: moving from H100->A100 increases units per 1M token by ~25–40% (matches Rafael's estimated bands).

I'll prepare the CSV with per-GPU throughput vs p95 latency and attach to the quote draft. Recommend we propose a 4-week pilot on H100 (discounted) then a 12-month reservation on H100 x4 if pilot meets SLA.

-Marissa
Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: rafael_mendes@redwood.com
To: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@brightanalytics.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, procurement@brightanalytics.com
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 14:38:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: dedicated capacity options — clarifying throughput & budget

Aisha — looping back with concrete asks and a proposed pilot + MAP. See below.

Proposed quick plan (assuming you pick Band A / H100 route):
1) Pilot (2–4 weeks) — H100 x1 (discounted): validate p95, KV caching impact, and burst handling. Target start: week of Nov 29.
2) Pilot success criteria (examples): sustained p95 < 400ms for 200-token responses at 80 rps sustained for 30m window; error rate < 0.5%.
3) Reservation proposal: H100 x4 reserved for 12 months (we'll provide phased billing options).
4) Approx ballpark pricing: pilot (pass-through) + reservation pricing that targets ~$500 per 1M tokens (we'll firm up in quote).

Docs attached: draft SOW, throughput CSV, and our standard reservation agreement template.

If that looks ok, can we schedule a 30-min procurement + engineering alignment for next Tue? Also please confirm whether BrightAnalytics requires an explicit PO before we proceed with pilot infra.

Best,
Rafael

Thanks Rafael — that plan looks sensible. Quick answers: 

- BrightAnalytics prefers Band A if the unit econ can be held at or below $600 / 1M tokens for the first 12 months. That's our internal threshold.
- Pilot: yes — please provision H100 x1 for 2 weeks starting Nov 29. We'll provide an NDA amendment and expect a short PO for pilot pass-through. Procurement contact is procurement@brightanalytics.com (cc'd).
- Timeline: procurement will need a draft quote/RA to review; if you can get a formal quote to us by Nov 20, we can target a Dec 1 reservation effective date after internal approvals.

I'll take the SOW to the legal and loop in Engineering for the procurement call next Tue.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — looking forward to the quote.

Aisha

BrightAnalytics
